tags.documentation: The identifier this reactor is known by on the wire and in every record: the topic form, lowercase -- br-201, br-202. Pattern 7 keys both of its lookups on this, as a literal against bes.batch_event.equipment_id and em.reading.equipment_id, and pattern 1's valve event carries it to the LIMS so a sample knows which vessel it came from. NOT plant.equipment's 'BR-201' -- that table is deliberately not on pattern 7's path and its casing does not match anything else in the stack. A memory tag for now; the obvious next step is a SQL lookup against an asset register, which is why it lives in its own folder rather than beside the process values.
tags.name: equipment_identifier

tags.documentation: The batch this reactor is running. Minted by bes_batch on the first advance out of IDLE and cleared when the batch ends -- not typed. A hand-typed id is how four conventions ended up live at once. Pattern 7 takes batch identity from bes.batch_event, which is where this is stamped on every row, NOT from the LIMS review message: every sample pattern 1 has actually minted carries an empty batch_id. Historised on change to pg-historian, which is what lets pattern 7 answer the same question over i3X: POST /objects/history on this reactor, last row at or before the sample instant, instead of a SELECT against bes.batch_event. Same fact, read through the vendor-neutral interface rather than through this gateway's own datasource.
tags.name: batch_id

tags.documentation: The bes.batch_event event_type of the INCOMING row of the last advance: operation_start, or batch_end on the advance that closes the batch. The outgoing operation_end row is deliberately not mirrored here -- both rows of an advance share one occurred_at and only the incoming one describes what is running now. Written by bes_batch AFTER the database commit, alongside operation, so the tag never leads the record. Exists only because bes.batch_event has it and the tag model did not: over i3X pattern 7 reads batch identity from history, and without this it cannot tell a live operation from the IDLE that a batch_end leaves behind.
tags.name: event_type

tags.documentation: THE trigger for pattern 5. Click it true in Tag Explorer and the reactor steps to its next ISA-88 operation: two rows into bes.batch_event in one transaction, and nothing onto MQTT. Debezium tails the table out of band and the message appears without this gateway asking for it -- which is the entire pattern. bes_batch resets this to false when it is done.
tags.name: manual_advance

tags.documentation: The ISA-88 operation currently running: IDLE | CIP | SIP | INOC | GROWTH | HARVEST. Written by bes_batch AFTER the database commit, so the tag never leads the record. An *operation*, not a phase -- a phase is the smallest process action ("Add Water", "Agitate"); CIP/SIP/INOC/GROWTH/HARVEST are one level up. The batch protocol qualifies sampling for GROWTH only, and that rule lives in bes_batch, not here. Historised on change, so "what was running at time T" is answerable from the tag model as well as from the table -- the history rows are the reactor's operation timeline, and the Explorer draws them without knowing Postgres exists.
tags.name: operation

tags.documentation: Whether the batch protocol qualifies sampling in the operation now running -- the same flag bes_batch stamps into bes.batch_event.payload for the incoming row, mirrored here so it can be read back. Derived from bes_batch.QUALIFIED, which stays THE ONLY COPY OF THE RULE: nothing downstream may test operation == "GROWTH" for itself. False on every batch_end, because nothing is running between a batch's last operation_end and the next batch's first start. Historised because the payload jsonb is not in the tag model at all, and over i3X history is the only way pattern 7 can see this flag.
tags.name: qualified_window

tags.documentation: Write true to run an analysis. This is the VENDOR's own trigger, not something added for the demo - the analyzer exposes no OPC UA methods at all, only writable bits. Set the sample metadata tags below FIRST: nothing here is atomic and the instrument reads them at the instant the bit goes true. There is also no refusal path - write it while an analysis is running and all that happens is nothing.
tags.name: esm_schedule_analysis

tags.documentation: Aborts a run in progress. State goes to 3 (Aborted) and the counter does not move.
tags.name: esm_terminate

tags.documentation: Applied to the NEXT analysis. Read the as-run value back from result/sample_id, never from here - this one is just the request.
tags.name: sample_id

tags.documentation: Degrees C, vendor default 37. The three temperature-corrected calculated results are identities at 37 - change this and watch them separate from their raw twins.
tags.name: vessel_temperature

tags.documentation: The vendor manual names and types this but never defines it. Treat with care.
tags.name: co2_saturation

tags.documentation: Bicarbonate, mmol/L.
tags.name: hco3

tags.documentation: Corrected to command/vessel_temperature. Equals ph at the default 37 C.
tags.name: ph_corrected

tags.documentation: How many images the density result was actually computed from - the closest thing the analyzer publishes to a confidence figure.
tags.name: good_image_count

tags.documentation: 10^6 cells/mL.
tags.name: total_density

tags.documentation: 10^6 cells/mL.
tags.name: viable_density

tags.documentation: mmol/L.
tags.name: ca

tags.documentation: Glutamine, mmol/L.
tags.name: gln

tags.documentation: Glutamate, mmol/L.
tags.name: glu

tags.documentation: Glucose, g/L - mass, not molar.
tags.name: gluc

tags.documentation: mmol/L.
tags.name: k

tags.documentation: Lactate, g/L - mass, not molar.
tags.name: lac

tags.documentation: mmol/L.
tags.name: na

tags.documentation: Ammonium, mmol/L.
tags.name: nh4

tags.documentation: Free text, empty when clean. Per-analyte failures also show up as Bad quality on the individual result tag below - the quality IS the error signal, which is the argument for OPC UA over a CSV that can only write a number.
tags.name: errors

tags.documentation: mmHg.
tags.name: pco2

tags.documentation: Unitless.
tags.name: ph

tags.documentation: mmHg.
tags.name: po2

tags.documentation: Not sample_time. Runs later if CDV images are reanalyzed or the result is edited after the fact - so a result CAN change after you have already read it. With no vendor completion counter that is a second reason polling cannot be trusted.
tags.name: modified_time

tags.documentation: The vendor's own absent-vs-zero mechanism, and the reason this folder is worth publishing: False here is Good and true - 'the osmometer did not take part in this analysis' - while result/osmo alongside it is Bad_NoData. Without this a consumer cannot tell 'not measured' from 'lost in transit'.
tags.name: osmo

tags.documentation: mOsm/kg. Bad_NoData whenever the osmometer is unfitted, which is the demo default. Bad is the correct answer here, not 0 - and modules_used/osmo says False, Good, beside it. See docs/reference/novaflex2-opcua-model.md section 8.
tags.name: osmo

tags.documentation: Which sampling path produced this - Manual, ESM, OLS, EXT_OLS.
tags.name: sample_source

tags.documentation: THE trigger for the MQTT publish. Vendor HistoricalSampleResults/SampleTime, written last by the simulator after every other historical leaf. A valueChanged script hands the result folder to event stream 03_opcua/cell-analyzer-result, which reads the sibling historical tags and publishes via Transmission. Do not point this at ICC26Extensions.
tags.name: sample_time

tags.documentation: The whole sample result as one JSON document, written in the same transaction as the leaves below. Read this instead of 39 tags when assembling the MQTT payload: it cannot tear across two samples, and it is one OPC read rather than 39.
tags.name: result_json

tags.documentation: Demo extension, not the MQTT trigger. The real instrument OPC server has no completion counter at all - SampleResults just changes underneath you. Pattern 3 publishes off result/sample_time (vendor HistoricalSampleResults/SampleTime). This node still increments last in ICC26Extensions so the gap is visible in the address space. A QC run and a failed analysis both leave this untouched. UInt32 on the wire, so Int8 here.
tags.name: sample_complete_counter

tags.documentation: 0 Idle, 1 Running, 2 Completed, 3 Aborted, 4 Error, 5 Calibrating, 6 QualityControl, 7 Maintenance. Also an extension: the vendor publishes no state tag, only ActiveTasks as free text.
tags.name: state

tags.documentation: Vendor liveness tag. Section 6 of the analyzer OPC manual tells you to subscribe to this and to the analyzer clock to confirm the server is updating at all - it is the vendor's own acceptance test, so it is worth having as a tag. It is a plain member here and not a nested object, deliberately, and it is not free: it ticks every 5 s, the i3X server re-sends an object's whole value document on any member change, so an idle subscription on this analyzer takes about 4.8 kB every 5 s to carry it -- measured 2026-09-19 as 12 pushes over 45 s with it, and 0 without. Splitting it into a nested UDT was tried the same day and does not help: the nested instance is still a member of this UDT, so its tick still wakes the parent, and the server strips the child from the payload only afterwards -- an unchanged document with a fresh timestamp. The fix belongs in the subscription listener, which should not push a value equal to the one it last pushed. See docs/plans/03-opcua-analyzer-i3x.md.
tags.name: uptime

tags.documentation: values.analyst -- who signed the review this assessment was made from.
tags.name: analyst

tags.documentation: values.assessed_at -- when sample_chain ran the assessment. ts against this is how old the fact was at the moment it was judged.
tags.name: assessed_at

tags.documentation: values.batch_id -- the batch from bes.batch_event, never from the review message, which carries none at all. Empty after a batch_end: the sample was drawn with no batch running, and that is worth recording rather than papering over.
tags.name: batch_id

tags.documentation: values.batch_context.operation -- the ISA-88 operation that was running at ts, from bes.batch_event or, with sample_chain.CONTEXT_SOURCE set to "i3x", from this reactor's own batch_data history. Null when no batch context could be resolved, and document carries the reason.
tags.name: batch_operation

tags.documentation: values.disposition -- the analyst's verdict on the sample, pass | fail, carried through from the review. A deviation can exist on a pass; a fail is one violation among several.
tags.name: disposition

tags.documentation: The whole pattern 7 envelope as sample_chain.build assembled it, system.util.jsonEncode'd, exactly as it went onto icc26/site1/qc/deviation. The scalars below flatten the parts a consumer queries on; the violations array and the full batch_context and environment blocks survive only here. Written by model_feed.write_deviation off the broker, NOT by pattern 7 itself -- 07 still publishes and nothing more, and its output reaches the typed model the same way any other i3X consumer's would.
tags.name: document

tags.documentation: values.environment.age_s -- how far the nearest cleanroom reading sat from ts, in seconds. Tens of seconds is the demo case; a large number means the room was last measured a long way from the sample, and the deviation says so instead of hiding it. Null when no reading was in range at all.
tags.name: environment_age_s

tags.documentation: values.environment.status -- normal | excursion for the cleanroom reading nearest ts, as particle_counter_poll computed it against config/excursion_threshold. Pattern 7 does no arithmetic of its own here. Null when no reading was in range.
tags.name: environment_status

tags.documentation: values.equipment_id -- the vessel, topic form (br-201). This object is one fixed instance rather than one per vessel: a deviation is an event, and the vessel it happened on is a field of it.
tags.name: equipment_id

tags.documentation: values.equipment_identifier -- the vessel's own asset_data/equipment_identifier, read back out of the tag model at assessment time. Identical to equipment_id today and deliberately kept as a second field: one is what the message said, the other is what the model says, and a mismatch between them is exactly the thing worth seeing. Null when the read failed, which is not itself a violation.
tags.name: equipment_identifier

tags.documentation: values.batch_context.qualified_window -- whether the batch protocol qualified sampling in that operation. Read, never recomputed: bes_batch.QUALIFIED is the only copy of the rule and pattern 7 does not hold a second one. Null when no batch context could be resolved.
tags.name: qualified_window

tags.documentation: values.sample_id -- the sample this deviation is about, the identifier pattern 1's valve minted. Every other record of this event joins on it.
tags.name: sample_id

tags.documentation: The envelope's ts -- the acquisition instant of the sample, carried unchanged from the review. Not when the assessment ran; that is assessed_at.
tags.name: ts

tags.documentation: values.violations[*].code, comma-joined, in the order sample_chain raised them. Each code's detail lives in full in document; this is the queryable form, so "every deviation that cited the room" is one history query rather than a scan through JSON strings.
tags.name: violation_codes

tags.documentation: values.analyst -- who approved or rejected it, as the LIMS recorded them. A LIMS login, not a gateway user, and not the person who badged the valve; see badge_holder.
tags.name: analyst

tags.documentation: values.collection.badge_holder -- who badged the sample valve in pattern 1. Two people, two systems, one sample: this one drew it, analyst signed for it.
tags.name: badge_holder

tags.documentation: values.collected_at -- when the LIMS recorded the sample as collected.
tags.name: collected_at

tags.documentation: values.collection.cycle_result -- the valve's own outcome for the cycle that drew this sample: normal, failed-to-seat, stroke-timeout. Pattern 7 raises a violation on anything but normal.
tags.name: cycle_result

tags.documentation: values.disposition -- pass | fail, the analyst's verdict on the sample. Pattern 7 treats a fail as one violation among several; a failed review is not by itself the deviation.
tags.name: disposition

tags.documentation: The whole pattern 4 review envelope, system.util.jsonEncode'd, exactly as it arrived on icc26/site1/qc/lims/sample-result. The scalars below are a flattened index into this string, not a replacement for it: a consumer that reads this one tag has everything the MQTT subscriber had, which is what makes the i3X path equivalent to the broker path rather than merely similar to it.
tags.name: document

tags.documentation: values.equipment_id -- the vessel this review is about, topic form (br-201). It is also what routed the review here: model_feed.write_review turns this id into a path under [default]icc26/site1/upstream/bioreactors and writes qc_data/last_review beneath it. REVIEWED, not raw: the LIMS resolved the vessel from pattern 1's topic, whereas the analyzer's own result knows it only from what somebody typed on the sample-login screen.
tags.name: equipment_id

tags.documentation: values.results[analyte == "glucose"].value, g/L -- mass, not molar, matching the analyzer's Chem/Gluc. Written as None when the analyte is absent, never skipped: the object's shape is fixed so a consumer can tell "not measured" from "never populated".
tags.name: glucose_g_l

tags.documentation: values.results[analyte == "lactate"].value, g/L -- mass, not molar. None when absent; see glucose_g_l.
tags.name: lactate_g_l

tags.documentation: values.results[analyte == "osmolality"].value, mOsm/kg. Usually None, and honestly so: the osmometer is unfitted in this demo, the analyzer reports Bad_NoData for it, and the LIMS has nothing to review. See glucose_g_l.
tags.name: osmolality_mosm_kg

tags.documentation: values.collection.sample_completion -- the valve's own completion time from pattern 1, carried through the LIMS unchanged. The same instant this vessel's process_data/sample_valve/last_sample_time holds, which is how the two ends of the chain are shown to agree without either end having been asked.
tags.name: sample_completion

tags.documentation: values.sample_id -- the identifier pattern 1's valve minted and every hop since has carried unchanged. The join key back to lims.sample and to this same vessel's process_data/sample_valve/last_sample_id.
tags.name: sample_id

tags.documentation: The envelope's ts: the acquisition instant this review is about, not when the review was typed -- that is verified_at. Pattern 7 keys both of its context lookups on this instant.
tags.name: ts

tags.documentation: values.verified_at -- when the analyst pressed approve. ts against this is how long the sample sat between acquisition and verdict.
tags.name: verified_at

tags.documentation: The stall demo. Uncheck it and particle_counter_poll returns immediately: the instrument keeps sampling on its own clock and the backbone goes silent, with nothing failing and nothing alarming. Re-enable it and the cursor walk drains the whole backlog in one burst -- hasMore, visible on the wire.
tags.name: enabled

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 0.5 um and larger channel above which particle_counter_poll writes status='excursion'. 1660 counts in the 4.717 L a 10 s sample draws at 28.3 LPM, which is 352,000 particles per cubic metre -- ISO 14644-1 Class 7, EU GMP Grade C at rest. **Chosen for DURATION=10.** Change the sample duration and this number silently means something else, with nothing in the system to catch it. That is the price of thresholding raw counts, and it is why the volume it was chosen for is written down here. Measured against the simulator on 2026-08-29: clean room 113-137 counts, dirty room 3346-4350, so the limit sits an order of magnitude clear of both. It applies to the 0.5 um channel ONLY. One raw-count number cannot also threshold the 5.0 um channel, whose ISO 7 limit is 2,930 per cubic metre -- about 14 counts at this volume, two orders of magnitude away. The 5 um count is published and stored so a consumer can see it; it is not compared here, because a second threshold would be a second copy of the cleanroom spec. THIS TAG IS THE ONLY COPY OF THE RULE.
tags.name: excursion_threshold

tags.documentation: Seconds between polls -- DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Nothing reads this tag. The cadence really lives in the 06-poll gateway timer's attributes.delay (30000 ms), because a timer's delay is fixed at resource load and no tag can change it live. Kept because the number is half of pattern 6's argument: the detection gap is the sample duration plus this, worst case, and it belongs on screen. Change it here and in ignition/timer/06-poll/resource.json together. For the stall demo use config/enabled, which the poll DOES read -- widening this tag does nothing.
tags.name: poll_interval_s

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 0.3 um and larger channel for the last analysis. Raw, not normalised -- see config/excursion_threshold for what that binds the number to.
tags.name: ch_0_3

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 0.5 um and larger channel for the last analysis. Raw, not normalised -- see config/excursion_threshold for what that binds the number to.
tags.name: ch_0_5

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 1.0 um and larger channel for the last analysis. Raw, not normalised -- see config/excursion_threshold for what that binds the number to.
tags.name: ch_1_0

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 3.0 um and larger channel for the last analysis. Raw, not normalised -- see config/excursion_threshold for what that binds the number to.
tags.name: ch_3_0

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 5.0 um and larger channel for the last analysis. Raw, not normalised -- see config/excursion_threshold for what that binds the number to.
tags.name: ch_5_0

tags.documentation: Raw particle count in the 10.0 um and larger channel for the last analysis. Raw, not normalised -- see config/excursion_threshold for what that binds the number to.
tags.name: ch_10_0

tags.documentation: Average flow rate over the analysis, LPM, from the vendor record's results.environment.flowRate.average. Nominal is 28.3 LPM and current/total_volume_l is this times the sample duration, so a drift here is what makes one analysis's raw counts mean something different from the next one's. Already stored in em.reading.environment and already on the wire; this folder is the third place, and it exists because POST /objects/history is the composite read path over i3X and a tag that is not in the model is a null column in every row.
tags.name: flow_rate_lpm

tags.documentation: Average relative humidity over the analysis, percent, from results.environment.humidity.average. Context, not a threshold -- see temperature_c.
tags.name: humidity_pct

tags.documentation: Average room temperature over the analysis, degrees C, from results.environment.temperature.average. Context, not a threshold: nothing in this stack compares it to anything, and config/excursion_threshold is the only cleanroom rule we hold. Here so an i3X consumer reading this object gets the same environment block the MQTT subscriber gets.
tags.name: temperature_c

tags.documentation: The operator's sample point, typed on the instrument's touchscreen at :8089 and carried in the vendor record's deviceName. The vendor record has no location field; this is that overload, named rather than hidden. If the vendor API ever grows a real location field, move it and delete this sentence.
tags.name: location

tags.documentation: Who the instrument says ran the analysis. The instrument's claim, not a gateway login.
tags.name: operator

tags.documentation: The instrument's own monotonic counter for this analysis. Published as the envelope's `seq`, exactly as pattern 5 publishes bes.batch_event.id -- the source system's number, never one we invent. It restarts at 1 when the simulator restarts, which is what makes the stale-cursor trap possible; see state/cursor.
tags.name: sequence_number

tags.documentation: normal | excursion. THE FLAG. Computed by particle_counter_poll at ingest from current/ch_0_5 against config/excursion_threshold, stored in em.reading.status and published as values.status. The instrument does not produce it and must never be asked to: the cleanroom limit is Ignition's rule and has exactly one home. Pattern 7 reads this flag and does no arithmetic of its own -- docs/00-architecture.md, 'Derived flags travel with the fact that produced them'.
tags.name: status

tags.documentation: Litres actually drawn by this analysis (about 4.717 L at 28.3 LPM for 10 s). Every raw count in this folder means something only against this number, which is why it goes on the wire too: a consumer can normalise to counts per cubic metre even though we did not.
tags.name: total_volume_l

tags.documentation: completedAt from the instrument -- the acquisition instant, not the instant we found out about it. state/last_poll_ts is the other half of that pair, and the distance between them is the detection gap.
tags.name: ts

tags.documentation: THE WATERMARK. The opaque cursor the instrument last handed back, base64 of an id. Written once per poll, after the last complete page, so a partial walk leaves it where the last whole page ended. It persists across a gateway restart -- value persistence on the `default` provider is Database -- so the poll resumes rather than replaying the buffer. **Clear this tag to recover from the stale-cursor trap.** Restart the simulator and its sequence numbers begin at 1 again while this still points past the end, so the server answers 'nothing after 45' -- correctly -- and the poll runs perfectly while publishing nothing, with every health check green. Emptying this string forces a replay.
tags.name: cursor

tags.documentation: Whatever the last poll hit -- the 401, the timeout, the connection refused -- or empty on success. **The stale-cursor failure writes nothing here**, and that is the whole point of it: the poll is working.
tags.name: last_error

tags.documentation: When the poll last ran -- not when the last analysis happened, which is current/ts. The two far apart with no error means the poll is healthy and the instrument is stopped; the two close together with a sequence_number that never moves means the cursor is stale.
tags.name: last_poll_ts

tags.documentation: The highest sequenceNumber this gateway has already stored and published. The dedupe guard: the poll skips anything at or below it, which is what makes re-reading a page after a mid-page failure safe and what stops a stale-cursor replay from publishing an analysis twice. Per-record, not per-page, deliberately. Persists with state/cursor and is cleared with it.
tags.name: last_sequence

tags.documentation: The valve cycle outcome: normal, failed-to-seat, or stroke-timeout.
tags.name: last_cycle_result

tags.documentation: Seconds since the last completed sample. The analysis trigger rejects stale retained events.
tags.name: last_sample_age_s

tags.documentation: The identifier minted by the sample valve and carried unchanged into downstream analysis.
tags.name: last_sample_id

tags.documentation: Completion time normalized to DateTime. Plain MQTT sends ISO-8601 text; Sparkplug B sends a typed DateTime.
tags.expression:
if(
	isNull({[.]last_sample_time_raw}),
	null,
	if(
		typeOf({[.]last_sample_time_raw}) = "String",
		toDate(
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 0, 4) +
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 5, 7) +
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 8, 10) + "." +
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 11, 13) +
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 14, 16) +
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 17, 19) +
			substring({[.]last_sample_time_raw}, 20, 23) + "+0000"
		),
		toDate({[.]last_sample_time_raw})
	)
)
tags.name: last_sample_time

tags.documentation: The transport-native completion time: String for plain MQTT, DateTime for Sparkplug B.
tags.name: last_sample_time_raw
